summary: Bars state VEDP site-readiness and expedited-review assistance for new data centers with anticipated peak demand of 25 MW or more, and directs state agencies on noise, backup generation, cooling water, siting, and cost allocation.
source_title: Executive Order 22 (2026): Establishing New Nation-Leading Standards and Initiatives to Implement the Virginia Data Center Accountability Framework and Responding to Unprecedented Risk from Artificial Intelligence
notes: Signed 2026-09-18 by Gov. Spanberger (p. 9). The 25 MW threshold limits state VEDP assistance (Sec. I.B.4, p. 5); it does not set local zoning rules.

summary: Board voted to consider a resolution pausing its final votes on data center and substation applications that require legislative approval for up to 12 months, retroactive to 2026-09-15.
source_title: Board Approves Process that Could Pause Legislative Data Center & Substation Applications
notes: Status disputed. County release says a resolution 'if approved, would pause' Board action. Supervisor Briskman's release of 2026-09-16 (https://www.loudoun.gov/DocumentCenter/View/222331/Statement---Loudoun-Board-Enacts-Pause-on-Data-Centers) says the Board 'voted Tuesday to enact a temporary pause' that 'takes effect immediately', with a resolution to memorialize it later. Coded proposed until the formal resolution is acted on. Vote 7-1-1 per Briskman release; separate 7-1-1 vote (Briskman opposed) for a grid-reliability substation exception. County release also lists possible exceptions for expiring statutory decision deadlines. Applications can still be filed and go to the Planning Commission; administrative (by-right) applications, including grandfathered cases, not affected. Formal resolution (agenda item 14p) deferred from Oct 20 to Nov 17, 2026: https://www.loudoun.gov/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/10938. County Attorney advised a blanket moratorium is not legal in Virginia.

summary: Supervisors Briskman and TeKrony introduced a proposal directing staff to prepare an amendment ending the 2025 grandfathering resolution; the Board instead voted unanimously to request a County Attorney legal opinion.

source_title: Res. No. 26-374: Initiate a Zoning Text Amendment to the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District
notes: Vote 7-0, Vega absent from vote (p. 2). Page 1 is dated June 9; the page 2 header says June 2, which appears to be a typo; county page also says June 9. This replaced an earlier initiation: Res. No. 26-125 (2026-03-03) was stopped by Directive DIR 26-11 (2026-05-19) and rescinded by this resolution. summary: Board adopted Ord. No. 26-67, limiting the overlay to properties that meet one of five eligibility pathways, barring requests to add property to its map, and making a Special Use Permit the route for other data centers in listed business, office, and industrial districts.
source_title: Ord. No. 26-67: DPA 2026-00006, Zoning Text Amendment to the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District
notes: Vote 8-0; motion Gordy, second Vega (p. 2). Redline deletes Sec. 32-509.02(1), which allowed the overlay on land near transmission lines of 115 kV or more and planned or zoned for office or industrial uses (attachment p. 1). When that clause entered the code not yet verified. Attachment keeps a DRAFT watermark and date placeholders; Board directed staff to insert the adoption date (p. 2). Effective date unresolved: the ordinance has no effective-date clause; a Development Services memo of 2026-10-16 (https://www.pwcva.gov/assets/2026-10/DataCenterSitePlanSubmissionsMemorandum.pdf) says effective 2026-12-21 with site plans accepted by 11:59 pm that day grandfathered; the county's ZTA page says adopted ZTAs generally take effect immediately (https://www.pwcva.gov/department/planning-office/zoning-text-amendments). No effective row yet. Pathways (Sec. 32-509.02(2)): four had an adoption-day deadline; the fifth covers listed applications, final site plans, and final plats accepted within 90 calendar days. The Planning Commission's 120-day window and 500-foot setback do not appear in the adopted text. County page: https://www.pwcva.gov/department/planning-office/dpa2026-00006-data-center-opportunity-zone-overlay-district-dcozod (final boundary map after 2026-12-21). Reporting only: a 3-5 failed motion to remove the 90-day window, per Virginia Business 2026-09-23 (https://virginiabusiness.com/prince-william-county-moves-to-end-by-right-data-centers/); overlay shrinks from about 9,698 to 3,641 acres, per Manassas Journal 2026-09-23 (https://manassasjournal.com/prince-william-county-approves-62-reduction-in-data-center-overlay/). Final acreage waits on the county's map.

summary: Board adopted data center zoning standards: size caps in some districts, distances from homes and Metro entrances, equipment enclosure, and pre- and post-construction noise studies.
source_title: ZO 112.1-2024-9 / ZO 112.2-2024-8: Adoption of an Amendment to Chapters 112.1 and 112.2 (Zoning)
notes: Keeps by-right permission (P) in C-3, C-4, and I-2 to I-6, under standards in Sec. 4102.6.A. Size caps: 40,000 sq ft in C-3 and C-4; 80,000 sq ft in I-2, I-3, and I-4; larger needs a special exception. No cap in I-5 or I-6. Buildings 200 ft from residential lot lines, ground equipment 300 ft or behind the building, 1 mile from a Metro entrance; lesser distances with special exception. Some law firm alerts say nearly all data centers need a special exception; that is a characterization, not ordinance language. Previous approvals: site plans accepted by 2024-07-16 reviewed under prior rules if approved by 2025-07-16. Vote 8-2 (Alcorn, Jimenez opposed) per reporting: FFXnow 2024-09-11 (https://www.ffxnow.com/?p=302557). Motion: https://www.fairfaxcounty.gov/dranesville/sites/dranesville/files/Assets/documents/pdf/2024-09-10_BOS%20Motion-Data%20Centers_Approval.pdf. 2021 zoning rewrite and earlier permissions not yet researched.
